question: Which of the following Biosphere Reserves is located in Madhya Pradesh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Panna Biosphere Reserve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Panna Biosphere Reserve** is located in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India, and is recognized as a significant biodiversity hotspot.
 
• It was designated as a **Biosphere Reserve in 2020** by UNESCO under the Man and Biosphere (MAB) Program.
 
• The reserve is famous for its **tiger population** and is home to the Panna Tiger Reserve, which was revived after a near extinction of tigers in the area in 2009.
 
• The Panna Biosphere Reserve is situated on the **Vindhya mountain ranges**, and the Ken River flows through it, adding to its ecological diversity.
 
• Besides tigers, the reserve houses a variety of flora and fauna such as **leopards, gharials, and Indian wolves**, along with rich vegetation like teak and sal forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manas Biosphere Reserve**

 
 
• Located in Assam, Manas Biosphere Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Project Tiger reserve.
 
• It is known for its **unique wildlife**, including the golden langur, pygmy hog, and Bengal florican.
 
• The reserve is a part of the Eastern Himalayan biodiversity hotspot and features diverse ecosystems such as grasslands and tropical forests.
 
 
 
• **Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• Situated in Uttarakhand, this reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and includes the **Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks**.
 
• It is known for its high-altitude biodiversity, including species like the snow leopard, Himalayan musk deer, and Himalayan tahr.
 
• The reserve is located in the **Western Himalayas** and is a popular destination for trekkers and nature enthusiasts.
 
 
 
• **Similipal Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• Located in Odisha, this reserve is known for its **dense forests, waterfalls, and rich biodiversity**.
 
• It is home to several endangered species like the Bengal tiger, Asian elephant, and Indian bison (gaur).
 
• The reserve is named after the Similipal Hills and is a part of the Eastern Ghats.
